caption: How a hi team works. People talk to the team in its Slack channel, or in the helper on the app's pages. The lead, Hermes, is the only agent that runs all the time: it agrees work with the people, keeps the specs and its memory, and writes briefs. It puts members to work only through the broker, part of hi on the team's machine, which checks each yes against the channel's log, keeps at most five ideas open, runs each member in a box of its own on a branch, has the reviewer check the work, and merges and releases. Each member is a role with its own instructions and what it has learned; each task is a fresh agent. Merged work is dev, shown on the preview; a release puts it on production after an owner's yes. Everything lives in the team's folder.
via: the Slack channel · the helper in the app

key.text: One team, one Slack channel, one machine. People never need to reach it.
The one agent that runs all the time; it talks with the people and never writes code.
Part of hi, outside the lead's box, so approvals, reviews, and releases can't be skipped.
A role that outlasts its tasks; each task is a fresh agent in a box, on a branch.
What the people try, and what they use. Only an owner's yes moves production.
